title: Canonical Weil structure on the constant coefficient object
statement: Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g_Y:Y\to Y$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for every ring $A$ the inverse image $g_Y^{-1}$ of the constant sheaf $A_Y$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $A$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (the inverse image of a sheafified constant presheaf is the sheafification of the pulled-back constant presheaf, which is again constant), so there is a canonical isomorphism $c_{A,n}:g_Y^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y$, inverse to the adjunction unit on constant sections. For $A=A_{E,n}$ these isomorphisms are compatible with the reductions $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$, and the limit over $n$ is a canonical isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}:g_Y^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ of the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Since $g_Y^{-1}$ is exact, $Lg_Y^*$ of the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] agrees with $g_Y^{-1}$ on these sheaves placed in degree $0$, which are objects of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. The *canonical Weil structure* on $E_Y$ is the pair $(E_Y,\theta_{E})$ with $\theta_E$ the image of $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ in the rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; it is an object of $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The canonical Weil structure on $(\Qlb)_Y$ is $(E,(E_Y,\theta_E))$ in the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], independent of the stage $E$ up to the canonical isomorphisms $E_Y\otimes_EL\cong L_Y$, under which $\theta_E\otimes_EL=\theta_L$. The forgetful functor $\operatorname{For}$ sends these objects to $E_Y$ and $(\Qlb)_Y$.
